source_name: Payten Slovenija (ASEE payments arm) – corporate site
why_relevant: Payten claims maintenance of 30,000+ POS terminals and ATMs across Slovenia with seven regional service centres, and builds bank-branded apps (e.g. NLB Smart POS Slovenija). Its site and app-store listings are direct evidence of who holds the acquiring/terminal-estate service contracts.

source_name: Temenos – Success Stories (Nova Ljubljanska Banka)
why_relevant: Named vendor success story documenting NLB's core-banking platform and the 2023 migration of N Banka (ex-Sberbank Slovenia) onto it — an award/scope record for the largest core-banking footprint in Slovenia.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld – Temenos T24 customer list
why_relevant: Third-party aggregated customer database naming banks per core-banking product; useful to enumerate Slovenian institutions on a given vendor stack and then hunt for the matching vendor press release.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf newsroom / investor releases
why_relevant: Global ATM/branch-automation vendor with installed base inside Bankart's Slovenian ATM fleet. Contract wins in small markets are usually only announced globally (or in SEC 10-Q segment commentary), so both the newsroom and EDGAR filings are worth tracking.

source_name: NCR Atleos – Newsroom and investor press releases
why_relevant: NCR hardware is a named component of the Slovenian ATM estate. Atleos publishes ATM-as-a-Service and bank outsourcing wins (e.g. Epirus Bank, Greece) that are a template for what a Slovenian award would look like; investor releases add materiality-tested detail. Ownership is in flux (announced Brink's acquisition), which itself changes the supplier landscape.

source_name: ATM Marketplace – vendor news aggregator
why_relevant: Trade-press aggregator that republishes ATM/self-service vendor contract wins across Europe, including small markets that never get a dedicated corporate press release. Good early-warning feed and a pointer to vendors' own releases.

source_name: Worldline Slovenia (sl-si locale site)
why_relevant: Worldline maintains a full Slovenian-language merchant-acquiring presence; its locale pages, support portal and partner/bank co-branding reveal which Slovenian banks it serves for acceptance and terminals.

source_name: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. (ex Intesa Sanpaolo Card) – company profile & filings
why_relevant: Nexi's Slovenian card-processing entity (Letališka cesta 29A, Ljubljana; formerly Intesa Sanpaolo Card) has no visible local pressroom, so registry/credit-profile aggregators are the practical evidence layer for its scale, revenue trend and bank ownership links — a proxy for contract volume.

source_name: Comtrade programske rešitve d.o.o. – Slovenian entity profile & site
why_relevant: Comtrade's Slovenian software entity (Letališka cesta 29B, Ljubljana; ~320 employees, ~EUR 33.5m revenue) is a significant local banking-IT integrator. Its own reference pages proved hard to surface via search, so the registry profile plus its named banking relationships is the current best entry point.

source_name: Marand d.o.o. – company site and Technology Park profile
why_relevant: Marand is a 30-year Slovenian ICT integrator whose banking references are not exposed through search; profile pages in the Technology Park Ljubljana directory and business registries are the practical starting point for confirming whether it holds banking-sector work.

source_name: Slovenian government contract-partner disclosure lists (vladna gradiva PDF)
why_relevant: Government contract-partner schedules enumerate Slovenian IT suppliers (RRC, MAOP, SRC, Unistar LC, S&T Slovenija, NIL, Smartis) with contract references. These are public-sector contracts, but they build the supplier actor map and confirm which integrators are capable of banking-scale core/system work.

source_name: openprocurements.com – Slovenian tender/award mirror by CPV
why_relevant: Third-party mirror of Slovenian public procurement indexed by CPV code (72500000 computer-related services, 48600000 database/OS software). Names winning IT suppliers, letting a supplier-side analyst reverse-map vendors to institutions and then search those vendors' own pressrooms.

source_name: Google Play / App Store publisher listings for banking-app vendors
why_relevant: App package names and publisher fields expose the actual software supplier behind a bank-branded app (e.g. com.payten.nlb.slovenia = Payten building NLB's Smart POS; com.halcom.mobile.hybrid.si.* = Halcom building bank mobile apps). This is award evidence that no press release provides, with dates from release history.

source_name: Bank-published counterparty documents naming the vendor (e.g. BKS Bank BizzNet terms, UniCredit Hal E-Bank manuals)
why_relevant: Slovenian banks' general terms (splošni pogoji) and user manuals for e-banking name the supplying vendor and product explicitly (Halcom Hal E-Bank / Web E-Bank / MultiPay at BKS Bank and UniCredit). This is the most reliable public proof of an installed vendor at a private bank where no tender exists.

source_name: Portal javnih naročil (Uradni list RS) – pregled objav, filtrirano po CPV/ponudniku
why_relevant: Official Slovenian public-procurement publication portal. Its 'Pregled objav' view accepts URL query filters (e.g. ?f=ponudnik:<maticna>|datum:YYYY,M,D-|cpv:66) which allows building payments-specific watchlists by CPV branch (66 financial, 30 card/equipment, 72 IT services) and by supplier registration number — the mechanism to catch card-processing, ATM, HSM and instant-payment procurements that never carry a 'banking' label.

source_name: Bankart – Flik product/scheme pages (Flik Pay, Flik POS, Flik e-commerce, EULA)
why_relevant: Documents the operational and contractual model of the domestic instant-payment scheme: merchants contract via a bank, Bankart supplies API keys, identifiers and integration documentation. Reveals the integration/vendor surface (PSPs, webshop integrators, POS suppliers) that surrounds Flik and therefore who competes for that work.

source_name: Flik.si – scheme site for consumers and legal entities
why_relevant: Scheme-level site (separate from Bankart corporate) listing participating banks/PSPs and merchant onboarding rules — the actor map for who is inside the domestic instant-payments scheme and thus who buys around it.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – plačilni sistemi / nadzor nebančnih ponudnikov plačilnih storitev
why_relevant: Central bank oversees BIPS/TIPS connectivity and supervises non-bank PSPs and FMIs; publishes payment-system operating reports and registers of notified payment institutions. Gives the authoritative actor list (acquirers, PSPs, e-money institutions) whose procurement is in scope, plus regulatory deadlines that trigger vendor selection.

source_name: AJPES – business register / financial statements (Bankart and payments vendors)
why_relevant: Entity resolution backbone: matična številka, ownership, and annual accounts for Bankart and every candidate supplier/PSP. Required to link tender notices, Erar payments and press mentions to one legal entity, and to size the processor's cost base.

source_name: SDH – Slovenski državni holding, news and sale tenders (incl. Bankart ownership stake)
source_subtype: state asset manager announcements / divestment tenders
why_relevant: SDH published a public call for binding bids for a business share in Bankart d.o.o. — ownership-change events reshape the processor's procurement posture and are announced here before any operational trace appears.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) – payment/card committees, annual report, terminski plan
why_relevant: Industry association whose payment-transactions, card-business and SWIFT committees coordinate cross-bank programmes (the layer where joint decisions precede joint procurement via Bankart). Annual reports and committee agendas expose upcoming scheme/regulatory workstreams.

source_name: European Payments Council – Slovenia instant-payment environment insight
why_relevant: Documents that in 2018 all Slovenian PSPs agreed to establish Flik as the domestic instant-payment scheme and tracks SCT Inst adherence — the scheme-governance timeline that dates each national implementation programme and its vendor demand.

source_name: Cetis d.d. – card/document personalisation supplier (Celje)
why_relevant: The domestic incumbent in secure card personalisation and smart-card supply (won the ZZZS health-card personalisation tender, runs tachograph card issuance). Tracking its tender wins and product pages is the cheapest proxy for the Slovenian card-personalisation and HSM/PKI procurement cycle, which never uses banking CPV codes.
